note: MAX_STRING_BYTES = 65536 appears in the limits table of BOTH canonical.py and js/src/canonical.js, under a comment in each promising the other carries the same table. Python's _check_shape applies it to every string and every object key. js/src/canonical.js declares the constant on line 52 and never reads it again -- grep the file: MAX_STRING_BYTES has exactly one occurrence. So a receipt whose only sin is a 65537-byte string loads under `npm i obsign-verify` and is refused by `pip install obsign-verify`, which is the class of split the table was written to close. The npm parser is the wrong one, and the vote is not close: the Rust crate, a third reading by another author, refuses it too, and the limit is stated as part of the format by the comments in both JavaScript and Python.
